_comment: The published price of credit. This file is the single source: domain.js, the application form and the prose on the site are all checked against it by scripts/check-rates.mjs, so a change here is a change everywhere or CI fails. Served publicly on purpose — these rates are published.

terms._comment: Weeks to flat interest percent, applied once to the principal and never compounded.

overdue._comment: Applies when a loan passes its final due date, after the grace days below. The penalty REPLACES the term rate rather than adding to it, and never reduces what is owed: going overdue can cost more or cost the same, never less.
overdue._ladderComment: Decided 27 November 2026, replacing the flat 35% of 3 November. A flat penalty sat below the 55% charged for the eight-week term, so on K4,000 a four-week loan that defaulted cost K5,400 for ever against K6,200 for borrowing eight weeks honestly — defaulting was K800 cheaper at any point past week four, and an overdue eight-week loan carried no late charge at all however long it ran. A ladder fixes both without punishing somebody who is briefly late: 35% to day 27, 45% from day 28, 55% from day 56, and so on. It passes the honest eight-week price at day 56, so defaulting stops paying after two months instead of never.
overdue._graceComment: Three days. Somebody whose salary lands late should not owe K1,040 more for it. The charge is all-or-nothing on day four, which is the cost of keeping one number a borrower can be told over the phone.
overdue._capComment: Interest stops at the principal, so the most anybody can owe is twice what they borrowed — the in duplum rule applied across the region. No longer dormant: the ladder reaches it after about seven steps, roughly six and a half months overdue. Confirm against whatever cap the Bank of Zambia sets under the Banking and Financial Services Act No. 9 of 2026 before relying on it.

legacy._comment: Loans signed before this file existed carry their own late terms in the record's late_payment_rate field, written at signing (7.5% per week overdue, additive, entered by staff). Those agreements are binding as signed. The engine never applies the ladder above to them.

2026-11-03._comment: The terms in force from 3 November to 27 November 2026: a flat 35% however long the delay. Loans signed in that window are priced by this block for the rest of their life. Their agreement says a flat 35% and that is what they pay; see av_rates_overdue_for_version().
2026-11-03._graceComment: Three days, not the zero the engine actually applied while these terms were in force. legal.php has promised “a grace period of three days applies before any late charge” since 3 October 2026, a month before these terms were set, so every loan signed under them was signed against that promise. Honouring it charges less than the engine did, never more, which is the only kind of change that is safe to make to an agreement without asking.
